english.title: Consume intoxicating liquor contrary to requirement by constable
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement imposed on you by a constable, not to consume in a designated public place, namely **(..SPECIFY..), something which was, or which the constable reasonably believed to be, alcohol
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(2)(a) and 12(4) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

english.notes:
From 20th October 2014, the power to make an order under section 13(2) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001 (power of local authority to designate public place for restrictions on alcohol consumption) is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to an order made before that date or anything done in connection with such an order. As such, this offence can still be committed in a public place designated by an order made before 20th October 2014.

As from 08/04/2013 Penalty Notices for Disorder may ONLY be issued to offenders aged 18 years or over.

This offence may be disposed of by the issue of a Penalty Notice for Disorder - PND Code DB07.

(i) A constable who imposes a requirement on a person under section 12(2) shall inform the person concerned that failing without reasonable excuse to comply with the requirement is an offence
(ii) The Penalty Notice for Disorder was raised from £50 to £60 as from 1/07/13.
(iii) The requirement may also by made by a PCSO although the legislation has never been amended and therefore PCSO not in text of wording)
